title: Shift shortcut mapping with key mapping is not working as expected (maybe :)

status.label: Check the Numpad Delete workaround on current stable
status.detail: On PowerToys 0.88.0, Shift+Numpad decimal reportedly does not trigger a shortcut that types a comma; a commenter suggests mapping Numpad Delete to comma with NumLock on.

judgment.rationale: The report lists PowerToys 0.88.0 and says Shift(left)+Numpad period does not trigger its comma-text shortcut, while the key without the remap types a comma. A commenter reports that with NumLock on, Shift+Numpad period emits Numpad Delete and that mapping Numpad Delete to comma achieves the desired result. That is a concrete possible workaround, but the reporter has not confirmed it and there is no current-build test. Ask whether the workaround resolves the report on v0.102.3001 before proposing a code change.
evidence: The reporter lists PowerToys 0.88.0 and a shortcut mapping involving Shift(left)+Numpad period to comma text.
The reporter says the shifted Numpad period produces no mapped output while the unremapped key produces a comma.
A commenter reports using NumLock on and mapping Numpad Delete to comma because Shift+Numpad period becomes Numpad Delete on their setup.
The issue has one comment, no assignees, and no current-version confirmation.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether mapping Numpad Delete to comma works on v0.102.3001 with NumLock on, and whether the original shortcut mapping still fails.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report is from 0.88.0 and a commenter provided a possible NumLock/Numpad Delete workaround that the reporter has not tested; determine whether the current behavior remains before selecting a product fix.

issue_context.summary: Shift+Numpad period reportedly fails to trigger a comma-text shortcut; a commenter suggests mapping Numpad Delete to comma with NumLock on.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.88.0 and expects Shift(left)+Numpad period to type a comma.
The reporter says the remapped shortcut does nothing, while the unremapped Shift+Numpad period produces a comma.
A commenter says their workaround was mapping Numpad Delete to comma with NumLock on because Shift+Numpad period becomes Numpad Delete.
inferences: The physical key event may change from Numpad period to Numpad Delete when Shift is held, but that behavior is reported by a commenter and may depend on the keyboard/NumLock state.
issue_context.analysis: The issue may be explained by the key identity changing under Shift rather than a failure to apply the selected shortcut. Ask whether the reported Numpad Delete mapping resolves this configuration on current stable.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body and its sole comment, including the concrete alternate mapping/workaround.
No current-build reproduction or reporter response confirming the workaround is available.

information_gaps.information: Whether mapping Numpad Delete to comma with NumLock on works on v0.102.3001, and whether the original Shift+Numpad-period mapping still fails
information_gaps.why_needed: The commenter reports that Shift changes the emitted key identity; confirming the workaround distinguishes configuration/input semantics from a current Keyboard Manager defect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On v0.102.3001 with NumLock on, try the existing mapping and the suggested Delete (Numpad)-to-comma mapping; report which physical input is captured and whether comma is emitted.

actions.label: Check the Numpad Delete workaround on current stable

comment.body: Thanks for the Shift+Numpad-period example. A commenter reports that with NumLock on, this keypress becomes Numpad Delete and that mapping `Delete (Numpad)` to comma works for them. Could you try that on v0.102.3001 and confirm whether it resolves your case, or whether the original mapping still fails?
